'''Jiun-ji''' (慈雲寺) is a [[Myoshin-ji School of Rinzai Zen|Myōshin-ji sect]] Buddhist temple located in [[Shimosuwa]], Nagano Prefecture, Japan. The temple's mountain name (''sangō'') is '''Hakugazan''' (白華山), and its principal object of worship is the [[Ekādaśamukha|Eleven-Faced Avalokitesvara]].

== History ==
Jiun-ji was established in [[1300]] (Shōan 2) as part of the [[Kencho-ji School of Rinzai Zen|Kenchō-ji school]] lineage. It was founded by [[Yishan Yining|Issan Ichinei]], with [[Kinasa Mitsusada]], the head priest of [[Suwa Taisha Lower Shrine]], as its patron. Issan was succeeded by Setsusun Yūbai, and the temple became a prominent Zen center in the region.

Jiun-ji played a significant role in the region's religious and cultural history, serving as the ''shuchū'' (headquarters) for local Zen temples. It was favored by [[Takeda Shingen]]{{efn|Japanese feudal lord (1521–1573)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takeda Shingen|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, who admired the temple's seventh abbot, Tenkai Genchō, and adopted the temple's crest, the Takeda clan's diamond-shaped emblem.

== Cultural Properties ==
* '''Nagano Prefectural Treasure'''
** '''Temple Bell''' - Cast in 1368 (Ōan 1). The bell measures 114 cm in height and 66.4 cm in diameter.
* '''Town-Designated Tangible Cultural Properties'''
** '''Main Hall''' - Rebuilt in 1808 (Bunka 5) by master carpenter Ichizō of Suwa. Constructed in the [[Tatekawa style]].
** '''Sanmon Gate''' - Built in 1779 (An'ei 8) by carpenter Chōzaemon Murata.
** '''Amitabha Buddha Standing Statue''' - Carved by Mokujiki, standing 112 cm tall, dated to 1807 (Bunka 4).
** '''Memorial Pagoda for Hineno Takayoshi''' - A five-ring pagoda commemorating Hineno Takayoshi, the first lord of the Suwa Domain.

== Access ==
* The temple is approximately a 15-minute walk from [[Shimo-Suwa Station|Shimosuwa Station]] on the JR [[Chūō Main Line]].
